also: let’s put this off to another time

terms.grammar: verb, irregular; in with the accusative of the new time: in crāstinum, in aliud tempus
evidence: Caes. BC 1.86: sī in aliud tempus differētur (Lewis & Short s.v. alius)
Cic. Rep. 2.44: reliqua in crāstinum (differre; Lewis & Short s.v. differō)
Traupman 106: let’s put this off to another time, hanc rem in aliud tempus differāmus
terms.comment: Literally “carry apart”. The new time goes into the accusative with in: in posterum diem, to the next day (Cic. Deiot. 21, Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Hanc rem in aliud tempus differāmus.
phrases.english: Let’s put this off to another time.

phrases.latin: Differāmus in crāstinum; jam sērō est.
phrases.english: Let’s put it off till tomorrow; it’s late now.
Do it tomorrow, do it the day after.

phrases.latin: sed, sī placet, in hunc diem hāctenus; reliqua — satis enim multa restant — differāmus in crāstinum.
phrases.english: but, if you like, that’s enough for today; let us put off the rest (for there is plenty left) till tomorrow.

phrases.latin: remque commōvistī novā disputātiōne dignam, quam in aliud tempus differāmus
phrases.english: you have raised a question worth a new discussion, which let us put off to another time

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 106, 337, 395.
